_note: Every upgrade the player can be offered. `source` decides which pool it enters: "levelup" is the ordinary in-run draw, "shop" is feed-priced and run-defining, "both" appears in either. `maxStacks` caps how many copies one run can hold. `cardSprite` is the atlas key the card art window draws; `_mockArt` is the design-review path only and can be stripped on import.
_designNote: Rarity spread is 11 common / 11 uncommon / 9 rare / 5 epic / 4 legendary. Commons are one plain number and are named after the object; legendaries change how a run plays and are named like they are spoken about. Every epic and legendary is shop-only, so the shop is where a run gets its shape.

_categoryNote: SS7.1: `category` is DECLARED, never sniffed. The draw quotas its board on it (at most one `stat`, at most one `merge`, one gated slot, one behavioural slot), and a draw that guesses its own quotas changes meaning every time a card gains a field. `tags` is SS4: the draw biases toward tags the build already holds, so a build FORMS instead of accumulating. Both are content; offers.ts reads and never infers.
_gateNote: `requiresLoad`, `requiresWeapon`, `requiresClass` and `requiresItem` are the gates that make the pool GROW through a run instead of shrinking. A gated card costs the early game nothing because it cannot appear yet, and it is where two runs stop looking alike. `requiresLoad` was batch 1's (the four Load Riders). Batch 2 turns on `requiresWeapon` for real: the 48 weapon-upgrade cards below plus the Smudge Pot's own three, each also carrying `weaponMod` -- the short id `Player.addItem` pushes onto that weapon's `WeaponSlot.mods` and `hasMod(slot, id)` reads back in `behaviours/weapons.ts`. `requiresClass` is still batch 4's.
_weaponModNote: docs/UPGRADE_ROSTER.md batch 2, SS6 (Weapon Upgrades) plus the Smudge Pot's own three, authored here because the doc predates that weapon. Rarity ladder uncommon/rare/epic at cost 20/30/44, `maxStacks: 1`, `source: "both"`, `category: "weaponMod"` -- all per SS6's table. Each carries a static `cardSprite` at the owning weapon's T1 art (weaponCardSprite(id, 1), computed once and pasted in rather than resolved live) -- zero new generations, exactly as SS10 plans, and it satisfies tests/content.test.ts's own rule that every cardSprite is a packed atlas key. OfferPool.itemOffer still falls back to weaponCardSprite off requiresWeapon for any future item that omits one. The magnitudes are not repeated here -- they live in weapons.json beside the tier riders they sit next to, at `<modId><Field>`, which is what lets behaviours/weapons.ts read hasMod(slot, 'chokeTube') beside tier >= n without a second source of the same number.
_stackNote: SS5, the card-text contract. `stackBlurb` is the behavioural card's answer to "what does taking this AGAIN do": `{n}` is the copy being offered and `{total}` is `n x stackPer`, so a card whose whole effect is prose still prints its number at the stack the player is looking at. A card with no `stackBlurb` falls back to `blurb`, which is what every stat card wants -- its numbers are in the delta line already.
_atlasNote: _atlas marks the cardSprite values art/sprites.json cannot resolve today. NEW ATLAS KEY (18): needs an itemIcons entry and, for most, new art — see SPRITE_REQUESTS.md. FRAME PICK (7): the clip is already packed and only needs a named frame exported as an icon. Everything unmarked resolves against sprites.json as it stands.
_artNote: Items flagged `_standInArt` borrow a sprite that means something else; they are the 'Still open' list in the design handoff and want real art. Everything else points at generated PixelLab card art (see docs/PIXELLAB_MANIFEST.md) or at a sprite the game already owns.
_standInNote: The 22 cards batch 1 adds all point at art the atlas ALREADY holds -- a salt rock for Rock Salt, an oil drum for Tar Load, a grave marker for Last Rites, a burning barrel for Hot As It Comes. That is deliberate and it is debt, recorded rather than hidden: SS10 lists 19 icons it wants generating for these, and none of them block the cards from shipping legibly. Nothing here borrows a sprite that means something contradictory on the field.
_retuneNote: docs/UPGRADE_ROSTER.md SS6 authored these numbers; tools/balance.ts then measured them, and they came in UNDER the stat cards they displace. That matters more than it sounds: the redesign deliberately cuts the stat share of the stream from 65% to 25%, so every behavioural card has to be worth roughly the percentage it is standing in front of, or the roster is a downgrade dressed as variety. Raised here: splitShot 45 -> 60%, moonshineJug 15/55 -> 20/70, broadSide 12 -> 15%, weakSeam 20 -> 28%, broodyHen 9 -> 14 damage, bloodMeal 1.2 -> 1.5, rotUnderfoot 14 -> 20 dps, lastRites 40 -> 55%. SS9 reserves a full retune for batch 5; this is the part of it the harness would not let wait.
_rangedGateNote: A gate was TRIED here and measured worse, which is worth more written down than left out. The five On-Hit cards that only touch a bullet were gated on owning a gun (requiresWeaponType: ranged), because The Hand opens with a pitchfork and five of the seven On-Hit cards cannot fire for him -- a real hole and exactly what SS3 says gates are for. On tools/balance.ts over 24 seeds x 3 pilots The Hand cleared 23/72 with the gate and 28/72 without it: gating cards OUT shrinks the early pool, so slot C falls further down its fallback chain and the board memory bites harder on what is left, and both cost more than the dead cards did. The reading offers.ts needs is still there and batch 2 is where it belongs -- that batch adds 48 weapon-gated cards, so the pool GROWS as it gates rather than shrinking, which is the condition under which the argument actually holds.
